newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm on tight supply, gasoline up.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm on tight supply, gasoline up.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were slightly firmer on Wednesday with the supply/demand equation working in the seller's favour, traders said.
Gasoline markets were tight amid good demand. One Slovenian need from a French refiner was heard met from within the refiner's system while another Slovenian requirement was unmet.
Italian demand faced tight supply. "If you want unleaded gasoline with one percent benzene I am not sure where you are going to get it," one dealer said.
Supplies were unlikely from Northwest Europe as refiners would find it more profitable to fill recent tenders in Ghana and Argentina, one refinery-based player said.

Naphtha discussion centred on the latest tender from the Egyptian General Petroleum Company, which closed on Wednesday, for up to around five 25,000 tonne cargoes from each of Suez and Alexandria for each of six months.
Much of the Russian gas oil overhanging the market appeared mopped up, but more cargoes were seen to start June.
Big players had shifted material to Northwest Europe with at least three Med 0.05 percent cargoes seen heading there. Players were watching the arb to the East which seemed near reopening.
Traders said premiums for Russian were around cif $1.00/$1.50 basis Genoa. ENF90 premiums were seen around hi fob $2.50/$3.50.

Limited refinery and solid bunker demand kept Med fuel oil markets supported and prompt good quality cracked markets seemed tight. Poorer quality Russian cracked fuel cargoes were abundant with at least one unsold on the water.
